errors.text: The hypothesis makes Ostwald ripening and transfer of matter to larger particles the dominant mechanism, whereas the target mechanism is selective Au/Cu surface segregation followed by shell melting and evaporation.
It predicts an increase in average particle size through coarsening, conflicting with the observed approximately 22% size reduction caused by evaporation.
The proposed operating boundary omits the experimentally relevant onset near 673 K and introduces an unsupported claim that particles above 50 nm recover sluggish-diffusion behavior.
